conversation.content:
Good morning, I’m so glad you were able to come in today. My name is Maya Bennett—I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician here at the women’s clinic. I work with new moms who are navigating all the emotional ups-and-downs that can come after a baby arrives.

Today I’ll be using a short, well-validated questionnaire called the EPDS—short for the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale. It’s simply a way for us to hear how you’ve been feeling over the past seven days so we can be sure you’re getting the support you deserve. Everything we talk about stays confidential, and there are no right or wrong answers.

We’ll walk through ten questions together. I’ll ask each in everyday language rather than reading the medical wording, and you can answer in whatever way feels most comfortable. If at any point you need a break, just let me know.

Ready to begin? Here’s the first question:

Over the past week, have you still been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt harder to do?

I can still laugh sometimes—like when my sister sent me a silly meme yesterday—but it definitely doesn’t come as easily as it used to. Things that would’ve had me cracking up before just get a small chuckle now, if that.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah, I can still laugh a little—just not as much or as easily as before the baby.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to some stuff—like when my mom takes the baby for a walk and I get twenty minutes to sip a coffee in peace—but it’s not the same excitement I used to feel. Mostly I’m just hoping the next feeding goes smoothly.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. Yesterday she spit up a ton right after I fed her and I kept thinking I must’ve done something wrong—maybe I held her wrong or ate the wrong thing. I know rationally it’s normal baby stuff, but the thought still pops up.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll just be sitting there, everything calm, and suddenly I’m worried her breathing sounds different or that she’s too warm—stuff I can’t even explain to anyone else. It passes pretty quick once I check on her, but it keeps sneaking up on me.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not really panicky-scared—more like a little jolt of worry when the house gets too quiet and I think, “Is she still breathing?” It’s not a full-blown panic, just a moment of “oh no” until I peek in the crib.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days, yeah. I’ll be trying to fold laundry while she’s napping and suddenly think about the bottles that need sterilizing and the texts I haven’t answered, and it feels like I’m drowning in tiny tasks. I usually get through it, but it’s like I’m always one step behind.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Sleeping itself isn’t too bad—once I’m out, I stay out. But some nights my mind just keeps spinning about everything I didn’t finish or whether she’ll wake up early, and it takes me a while to settle.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel that way sometimes—like yesterday evening when she wouldn’t settle and my partner was still at work. I just sat on the couch with her on my shoulder and felt this heavy sadness out of nowhere. It lifts after a bit, but it keeps catching me off guard.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… I’ve cried a couple times this week. Once was when she wouldn’t latch and I felt like my body was failing her, and another time was just after a shower when I caught sight of myself in the mirror and felt like I didn’t recognize me anymore.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, nothing like that. I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 12: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary  
Date: [today’s date]  
Respondent: 2–3 wk postpartum mother, no self-harm ideation endorsed.

Symptoms endorsed (EPDS items paraphrased):
- Loss of pleasure/enjoyment (items 1, 2) – “can still laugh a little… not the same excitement.”
- Excessive self-blame/guilt (item 3) – attributes normal infant behavior to maternal failure.
- Anxious preoccupation (items 4, 5) – “jolt of worry” about infant breathing, quiet house triggers.
- Feeling overwhelmed (item 6) – “drowning in tiny tasks,” falling behind daily demands.
- Sleep-onset difficulty linked to racing thoughts (item 7).
- Sad / miserable mood with crying spells (items 8, 9) – episodes triggered by infant care stress or body-image distress.

Pattern: Sub-syndromal depressive and anxiety symptoms, situational tearfulness, no anhedonia or pervasive low mood, no safety concerns.

Screening significance:  
Score range suggests mild-to-moderate postpartum distress; meets partial criteria for Minor/Sub-threshold Depression and Generalized Anxiety, not Major Depression. Continue monitoring; consider fuller assessment if symptoms persist >2 wks or worsen.
